summary: Sporting News' Week 14 standard-scoring fantasy football running back rankings, published ahead of the fantasy playoffs. It names the top RBs, waiver-wire sleepers, potential busts, and key injuries, including Derrick Henry, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jonathan Taylor. A full ranked list of 63 backs with matchups closes the piece.
one_line: Sporting News ranks Week 14 standard-league fantasy running backs, with sleepers, busts and injury updates, led by Christian McCaffrey at No. 1.
key_facts: Only the Cardinals and Commanders are on bye in Week 14, removing Brian Robinson Jr., James Conner and Antonio Gibson.
Christian McCaffrey (49ers vs. Seahawks) is ranked No. 1 after running for 139 yards and two TDs against Seattle on Thanksgiving.
Austin Ekeler is No. 2 vs. the Broncos despite just 2.99 yards per carry since returning from injury eight games ago.
Travis Etienne Jr. (Jaguars @ Browns) is ranked No. 3; Kyren Williams put 112 total yards and a TD on Cleveland in Week 13.
Detroit's David Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs combined for 193 yards and two TDs against Chicago in Week 11, and Miami's Raheem Mostert and De'Von Achane both rank in the top 10.
Houston has allowed 111.8 scrimmage yards per game to RBs and 14 total rushing TDs, so Breece Hall (vs. Texans) is ranked No. 7.
Tyjae Spears is the top waiver pickup because Derrick Henry suffered a head and neck injury in Tennessee's Week 13 loss to the Colts; Spears had 88 yards on 4.7 yards per carry.
Ezekiel Elliott gets lead-back duties for the Patriots after Rhamondre Stevenson's ankle injury; Stevenson will miss multiple weeks.
Keaton Mitchell has 330 yards and two TDs since breaking out four games ago but has yet to see 12 touches in a game.
Busts flagged: James Cook (2.7 yards per carry vs. the Eagles), Zach Charbonnet (knee bruise), Jerome Ford, Kareem Hunt, Chuba Hubbard and Miles Sanders.
Jonathan Taylor had thumb surgery and is expected to miss a few weeks; Zack Moss has posted multiple top-10 performances.
Kenneth Walker III (oblique) missed Weeks 12 and 13, and DeeJay Dallas would lead Seattle's backfield if Walker and Charbonnet are both out.
Aaron Jones has a sprained MCL and is week-to-week for Green Bay.
Rankings are for standard, non-PPR scoring and list 63 running backs, ending with Jamaal Williams.
